$comment: CI-only SecretLoop configuration. The self-scan job copies this to .secretloop.json before scanning, so the tool does not fail its own build on the synthetic credentials its tests generate on purpose. This is deliberately NOT the project's user configuration: a developer running `secretloop scan` locally still scans everything, which is what keeps the scanner honest about its own repository.
$comment_scope: Named files, not tests/**. Excluding the whole directory meant a real credential committed anywhere under tests/ passed CI silently — and every future test file was exempt the moment it was created. Listing the files that carry fixtures inverts that: a new test file is in scope by default, and adding one here has to be a deliberate act. src/, .github/ and everything else stay in scope as before.
$comment_detection: tests/detection.test.ts carries fixture passwords containing punctuation -- the exact values the 0.1.1 capture-class fix exists to catch. The self-scan finding them is the fix working, not a leak. Listed by name like every other fixture-bearing file rather than annotated inline: the whole file is detection fixtures, and ten inline directives would be noise that also suppresses the suppression count the same release added.
$comment_maintenance: If CI fails on a test file not listed here, that is the mechanism working. Check whether the finding is a fixture or a real credential before adding the path.
$comment_sarif: results.sarif is a SecretLoop report, not source. A scan output must never be a scan input: it contains every finding the previous run made, so scanning it re-reports each one as a fresh credential in a new file. Observed on the real-noise corpus, where a stray results.sarif contributed 4 findings of its own. From 0.1.1 the shipped defaults exclude **/*.sarif as part of the generated-file group, so this entry is belt-and-braces for a CI run that passes --include-generated.
$comment_bench: bench/ plants credential-shaped values on purpose -- its generators carry the format templates and its labels file records where each plant goes. Same reasoning as the fixture files above: the self-scan would otherwise fail on synthetic data the benchmark exists to produce. Scoped to the directory because everything in it is generator input, unlike tests/ where only some files carry fixtures.
